Self-taught lessons:
- Cost scale ~0.11 M/yr per mol/s at 40st R=6; a single column with R=6/60st cost $244.6M/yr.
- Revenue = flow * 2.88e7 * price. Pure nC4 (450 mol/s) = 166M/yr, but nC4 boils 272.7K vs iC4 261.3K — hard split.
- Blend prizes: C6 paraffin 1182, C5 mix 618, C6 naphthene 396, C4 mix 186, C3 mix 73. All need near-perfect multi-cut separation => many tall/high-reflux columns, far exceeding revenue at this cost level.
- Single-column cuts can't reach 95% on any blend: e.g. a C4/C5 split tops is only ~63% C4 because C3- remains; a C3/C4 split tops carries C2 impurity (~11%).
- Side draw must not sit on the feed stage (30 for a 60-stage column); that caused two rejections.

Conclusion: with only 2 solves and no evidence any real column beats 0.000, the empty plant (reward 0.000) is my best valid result. Reverting and finishing.
